
#MCPcounter in all cases HPV-I by p53 status

```{r}
library(coxphf)
library(knitr)
library(openxlsx)
library(immunedeconv)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(survival)
library(dplyr)
library(survminer)
library(edgeR)
```

```{r}
# convert to matrix (important for many bioinformatics tools)
counts_mat <- as.matrix(counts_HPV_Independent)

# remove duplicated gene symbols if any
counts_mat <- counts_mat[!duplicated(rownames(counts_mat)), ]

# create edgeR object
dge <- DGEList(counts = counts_mat)

# TMM normalization (library size normalization)
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)

# CPM expression matrix
cpm_mat <- cpm(dge, log = FALSE)
```


```{r}
mcp_counter <- deconvolute(cpm_mat, "mcp_counter")
length(mcp_counter$cell_type)


mcp_counter_long <- mcp_counter %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -cell_type, # All columns except `cell_type`
    names_to = "Sample", 
    values_to = "Fraction"
  )

analysis_data <- mcp_counter_long %>%
  left_join(TP53status_clinical, by = c( "Sample"="id"))
```

```{r}
length(unique(analysis_data$cell_type))
```

#PCA
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Step 1: Filter out unwanted scores
analysis_data_filtered <- analysis_data 

# Step 2: Convert long to wide format (samples = rows, cell types = columns)
pca_data <- analysis_data_filtered %>%
  select(Sample, cell_type, Fraction) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = cell_type,
    values_from = Fraction,
    values_fill = 0  # fill missing fractions with 0
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Sample")  # samples as rownames

# Step 3: Ensure all columns are numeric
pca_data[] <- lapply(pca_data, as.numeric)

# Step 4: Perform PCA
pca_result <- prcomp(pca_data, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Step 5: Extract PCA scores
pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca_result$x)
pca_df$Sample <- rownames(pca_df)

# Optional: add metadata for coloring
metadata <- analysis_data %>%
  select(Sample, p53_ihc_status) %>%
  distinct(Sample, .keep_all = TRUE)

pca_df <- pca_df %>%
  left_join(metadata, by = "Sample")

# Step 6: Plot PCA
ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = p53_ihc_status)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of Filtered xCell Fractions",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(summary(pca_result)$importance[2,1]*100,1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(summary(pca_result)$importance[2,2]*100,1), "%)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1")
```

```{r}
explained_df <- data.frame(

)

explained_df
```

#Which clinical variables is more associated with variability? Linear models with PC
```{r}
merged_df <- merge(pca_df, TP53status_clinical, by.x = "Sample", by.y = "id")

# We have two p53 status, Keep the x version
merged_df$p53_ihc_status <- merged_df$p53_ihc_status.x

merged_df$p53_ihc_status <- relevel(factor(merged_df$p53_ihc_status), ref = "Wt")
merged_df$tumor_size_category <- relevel(factor(merged_df$tumor_size_category), ref = "≤25 mm")
merged_df$depth_invasion_category<- relevel(factor(merged_df$depth_invasion_category), ref = "≤5 mm")

# Load necessary packages
library(broom)

# Perform linear regression and tidy the results for each principal component (PC)
lm_results <- lapply(grep("^PC", names(merged_df), value = TRUE), function(pc) {
  # Fit the linear model with the specified clinical variables
  model <- lm(as.formula(paste(pc, "~ age + factor(figo_ini_ava) + factor(nodal_status) +factor(margins)+ factor(depth_invasion_category)+factor(tumor_size_category) + factor(p53_ihc_status)")), data = merged_df)
  
  # Tidy the model results
  tidy_model <- tidy(model)
  
  # Add the PC name to each tidy output for reference
  tidy_model$PC <- pc
  
  return(tidy_model)
})

# Combine all the results into one data frame
lm_results_df <- do.call(rbind, lm_results)

# View the results
head(lm_results_df)
```



```{r}
# Round numeric columns
lm_results_df_rounded <- lm_results_df %>%
  mutate(
    estimate   = round(estimate, 2),
    std.error  = round(std.error, 2),
    statistic  = round(statistic, 2),
    p.value    = round(p.value, 3)
  )

# Export to CSV
write.csv(lm_results_df_rounded, 
          file = "lm_results_HPV-I_p53_MCP.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)
```

#Variables contributing to PC1 and PC2?
```{r}
# Assuming pca_result contains the PCA object with loadings
# Extract the loadings for PC1 and PC2
loadings <- pca_result$rotation  # Loadings are in the rotation matrix

# Get the top 3 contributors to PC1 and PC2 (by absolute value)
top_PC1 <- head(sort(abs(loadings[, 1]), decreasing = TRUE), 3)
top_PC2 <- head(sort(abs(loadings[, 2]), decreasing = TRUE), 3)

top_contributors <- data.frame(
  Variable = c(names(top_PC1), names(top_PC2)),
  PC = c(rep("PC1", 3), rep("PC2", 3)),
  Loading = c(loadings[names(top_PC1), "PC1"], loadings[names(top_PC2), "PC2"])
)
top_contributors$Contribution_pct <- top_contributors$Loading^2 * 100


# Plot the top loadings for PC1 and PC2 as percentages
ggplot(top_contributors, aes(x = reorder(Variable, Contribution_pct), y = Contribution_pct, fill = PC)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("PC1" = "grey27", "PC2" = "grey50")) +
  labs(title = "Top Contributions to PC1 and PC2 (%)", 
       x = "Variable", 
       y = "Contribution (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), 
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),  # Adjust margins to reduce space
        axis.text = element_text(size = 8),  # Smaller axis text
        axis.title = element_text(size = 10), # Smaller axis titles
        panel.grid = element_blank())  # Remove grid for a cleaner look


```






```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# Step 1: Extract PCA scores (already in pca_hiv_df)
pca_scores <- pca_df  # Assuming PC1 and PC2 are already in here

# Step 2: Extract loadings (directions of variable contributions)
loadings <- pca_result$rotation[, 1:2]  # Only PC1 and PC2

# Step 3: Get top contributing variables to PC1 and PC2
top_vars <- unique(c(names(top_PC1), names(top_PC2)))  # Combine top contributors

# Scale loadings for visualization — use a constant or use your data's scale
loading_df <- as.data.frame(loadings[top_vars, ])
loading_df$Variable <- rownames(loading_df)


p53_colors_custom <- c(
  "Mutant" = "#7B3294",  # strong dark purple
  "Wt"     = "#008837"   # strong green
)


# Step 4: Create PCA plot with arrows (biplot-style)
ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = factor(p53_ihc_status))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  # Add arrows for variable loadings
  geom_segment(data = loading_df,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1 * 10, yend = PC2 * 10),  # scaled for visibility
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm")), color = "black") +
  geom_text_repel(data = loading_df,
                  aes(x = PC1 * 10, y = PC2 * 10, label = Variable), 
                  color = "black", size = 3) +
  labs(title = "PCA with Top Variable Contributions",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(summary(pca_result)$importance[2,1] * 100, 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(summary(pca_result)$importance[2,2] * 100, 1), "%)"),
       color = "p53 Status") +
  scale_color_manual(values = p53_colors_custom) +

  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggpubr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(ComplexHeatmap)


# ============================================================
# 1. Wilcoxon test per cell type + BH-FDR correction
#    (mirrors `results_hpv` / the corrected `results_p53` for xCell)
# ============================================================

# Ensure p53_ihc_status is treated as a factor
analysis_data$p53_ihc_status <- factor(
  analysis_data$p53_ihc_status,
  levels = c("Wt", "Mutant")
)

# Perform Mann-Whitney U / Wilcoxon rank-sum test for each MCP-counter feature
results_mcp <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(p53_ihc_status), !is.na(Fraction)) %>%
  group_by(cell_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n_wt      = sum(p53_ihc_status == "Wt"),
    n_mutant  = sum(p53_ihc_status == "Mutant"),
    p_value   = wilcox.test(Fraction ~ p53_ihc_status)$p.value,
    median_wt      = median(Fraction[p53_ihc_status == "Wt"], na.rm = TRUE),
    median_mutant  = median(Fraction[p53_ihc_status == "Mutant"], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across ALL MCP-counter features tested
    FDR = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  arrange(FDR)

# View all results
results_mcp


# ============================================================
# 2. Keep only FDR-significant cell types
# ============================================================

significant_results <- results_mcp %>%
  filter(FDR < 0.05)

significant_cell_types <- significant_results$cell_type

significant_data <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(cell_type %in% significant_cell_types) %>%
  left_join(
    significant_results %>%
      select(cell_type, p_value, FDR, median_wt, median_mutant),
    by = "cell_type"
  )


# ============================================================
# 3. Boxplot/jitter panel of FDR-significant cell types
#    (guarded: MCP-counter has few features, so this may
#    legitimately come back empty after correction)
# ============================================================

if (length(significant_cell_types) == 0) {

  message("No MCP-counter features reached FDR < 0.05 for p53 status within HPV-independent tumors.")

} else {

  analysis_data_significant <- analysis_data %>%
    filter(
      cell_type %in% significant_cell_types,
      !is.na(p53_ihc_status),
      !is.na(Fraction)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      cell_type = factor(cell_type, levels = significant_cell_types),
      p53_ihc_status = factor(p53_ihc_status, levels = c("Wt", "Mutant"))
    )

  # Check how many observations each cell type has
  print(table(analysis_data_significant$cell_type))

  plot_labels <- significant_results %>%
    mutate(
      cell_type = factor(cell_type, levels = significant_cell_types),
      FDR_label = paste0("FDR = ", format.pval(FDR, digits = 2, eps = 0.001))
    )

  mcp_p53plot <- ggplot(
    analysis_data_significant,
    aes(x = p53_ihc_status, y = Fraction, fill = p53_ihc_status)
  ) +

    geom_boxplot(width = 0.45, outlier.shape = NA) +

    geom_jitter(
      aes(color = p53_ihc_status),
      width = 0.08,
      size = 1.5,
      alpha = 0.65
    ) +

    facet_wrap(
      ~cell_type,
      scales = "free_y",
      nrow = 2,
      ncol = 4
    ) +

    geom_text(
      data = plot_labels,
      aes(x = 1.5, y = Inf, label = FDR_label),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      vjust = 1.5,
      size = 3.5
    ) +

    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Wt" = "#41AE76", "Mutant" = "#79419D")
    ) +

    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("Wt" = "#2B6B4A", "Mutant" = "#4F2E6F")
    ) +

    theme_minimal() +

    labs(
      title = "MCP-counter Cell Type Fractions by p53 IHC Status (HPV-independent)",
      x = "p53 IHC Status",
      y = "MCP-counter Score",
      fill = "p53 IHC Status",
      color = "p53 IHC Status"
    ) +

    theme(
      panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold")
    )

  print(mcp_p53plot)
}


# ============================================================
# 4. Heatmap: FDR-significant MCP-counter features only
#    (guarded the same way)
# ============================================================

significant_cell_types <- results_mcp %>%
  filter(FDR < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(FDR) %>%
  pull(cell_type)

print(significant_cell_types)
length(significant_cell_types)

if (length(significant_cell_types) == 0) {

  message("Skipping heatmap: no MCP-counter features reached FDR < 0.05.")

} else {

  heatmap_data <- analysis_data %>%
    filter(
      cell_type %in% significant_cell_types,
      !is.na(Fraction),
      !is.na(p53_ihc_status)
    ) %>%
    select(Sample, Fraction, cell_type, p53_ihc_status)

  print(table(heatmap_data$p53_ihc_status))
  print(table(heatmap_data$cell_type))

  data_grouped <- heatmap_data %>%
    group_by(cell_type, Sample) %>%
    summarise(Fraction = mean(Fraction, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  data_wide <- data_grouped %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Sample, values_from = Fraction) %>%
    column_to_rownames("cell_type")

  data_matrix <- as.matrix(data_wide)
  mode(data_matrix) <- "numeric"

  data_zscore <- t(
    apply(data_matrix, 1, function(x) as.numeric(scale(x)))
  )
  rownames(data_zscore) <- rownames(data_matrix)
  colnames(data_zscore) <- colnames(data_matrix)

  sample_metadata <- heatmap_data %>%
    distinct(Sample, p53_ihc_status) %>%
    filter(Sample %in% colnames(data_zscore))

  # Reorder metadata to exactly match heatmap columns
  sample_metadata <- sample_metadata %>%
    slice(match(colnames(data_zscore), Sample))

  stopifnot(sample_metadata$Sample == colnames(data_zscore))

  p53_colors_custom <- c("Wt" = "#008837", "Mutant" = "#7B3294")

  column_annotation <- HeatmapAnnotation(
    p53_ihc_status = sample_metadata$p53_ihc_status,
    col = list(p53_ihc_status = p53_colors_custom)
  )

  Heatmap(
    data_zscore,
    name = "Z-Score",

    row_names_side = "left",
    column_title = "Samples",
    row_title = "FDR-significant MCP-counter features",

    cluster_columns = TRUE,
    cluster_rows = TRUE,

    clustering_distance_rows = "manhattan",
    clustering_distance_columns = "manhattan",

    clustering_method_rows = "ward.D2",
    clustering_method_columns = "ward.D2",

    top_annotation = column_annotation
  )
}
```
